proposals.before: Huo Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changle Palace; some came and went through the edict gate by night, arrogant and unrestrained, and I fear they may gradually escape control.
proposals.after: Huo Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changxin Palace; some came and went through the edict gate by night, arrogant and unrestrained, and I fear they may gradually escape control.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長信宮 is Changxin Palace, not Changle (長樂) Palace.

proposals.before: Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changle Palace; some passed through the edict gate by night, arrogant, extravagant, and unrestrained—I fear they may gradually become ungovernable.
proposals.after: Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changxin Palace; some passed through the edict gate by night, arrogant, extravagant, and unrestrained—I fear they may gradually become ungovernable.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長信宮 is Changxin Palace, not Changle (長樂) Palace.

proposals.before: In Emperor Yuan’s time, Wu Zun of Chang’an submitted a memorial saying, ‘When your servant was young, I served as a petty clerk in the commandery residence and privately saw Emperor Xuan, then the imperial great-grandson, in the prison there.
proposals.after: In Emperor Yuan’s time, Zun, a commoner of Chang’an submitted a memorial saying, ‘When your servant was young, I served as a petty clerk in the commandery residence and privately saw Emperor Xuan, then the imperial great-grandson, in the prison there.
proposals.reason: 士伍 is a commoner/soldier status label, not the surname Wu; the personal name is 尊 (Zun).

proposals.before: Chancellor Xiao He and Imperial Clerk Zhou Chang respectfully deliberated with General Liu Ling, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Shusun Tong, and others: The Son of Heaven’s clothing for spring, summer, autumn, and winter should model the numbers of Heaven and earth and attain the mean of human harmony.
proposals.after: Chancellor Xiao He and Imperial Clerk Zhou Chang respectfully deliberated with General Ling, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Shusun Tong, and others: The Son of Heaven’s clothing for spring, summer, autumn, and winter should model the numbers of Heaven and earth and attain the mean of human harmony.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 將軍臣陵 (General Ling); the surname Liu is not in the source.

proposals.before: Also in his heart he knew the heir apparent had no factual guilt; doubly he pitied the great-grandson’s innocence; Ji selected a careful and honest female convict, ordered her to nurture the great-grand grandson, and placed him in a quiet, dry place.
proposals.after: Also in his heart he knew the heir apparent had no factual guilt; doubly he pitied the great-grandson’s innocence; Ji selected a careful and honest female convict, ordered her to nurture the great-grandson, and placed him in a quiet, dry place.
proposals.reason: Typographical duplication: 'great-grand grandson' should be 'great-grandson' for 曾孫.

decisions.reason: Chinese 通籍長信宮 names Changxin Palace; Changle would be 長樂宮, so the palace-name correction is required.
The literal likewise misrenders 長信宮 as Changle; Changxin is the accurate place name.

decisions.after: In Emperor Yuan’s time, Chang’an commoner Zun submitted a memorial saying, ‘When your servant was young, I served as a petty clerk in the commandery residence and privately saw Emperor Xuan, then the imperial great-grandson, in the prison there.
decisions.reason: 士伍 is a status term, not surname Wu, and 尊 is Zun; the proposal’s appositive is ungrammatical, so render as ‘Chang’an commoner Zun’.

decisions.after: Chancellor Xiao He and Imperial Clerk Zhou Chang respectfully deliberated with General Wang Ling, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent Shusun Tong, and others: The Son of Heaven’s clothing for spring, summer, autumn, and winter should model the numbers of Heaven and earth and attain the mean of human harmony.
decisions.reason: Chinese has only 將軍臣陵; Liu is invented and wrong. Yan Shigu identifies 陵 as Wang Ling, parallel to the other expanded names in this sentence.

decisions.reason: Chinese 曾孫 is great-grandson; ‘great-grand grandson’ is a typographical duplication and must be corrected.
